We need to cluster equivalent facts. Let's list each candidate with its meaning.

0: subject Canon EOS 600D instance of digital single-lens reflex camera. object type camera. So claim: 600D is an instance of DSLR camera.

10: same but subject_type camera model, object_type camera type. Relation same "instance of". Should be equivalent: same proposition, just type differences. Both say it's an instance of digital single-lens reflex camera. So 0 and 10 are duplicates.

Also maybe 22: relation "camera type" object "digital single-lens reflex". That's a different relation: "camera type" vs "instance of". Not equivalent.

Now manufacturer: 1 (manufacturer Canon). 11 same but types differ. 19 also same but object_type "organisation". So 1,11,19 are duplicates.

Date of release: 2 (date of release 7 Feb 2011). 12 (release date same). 20 (date of release same). All equivalent.

Megapixels: 3 (megapixels 18.0 megapixel). 13 (megapixels object "18.0" with unit qualifier). 21 (megapixels object "18.0" with unit qualifier). 3 includes unit in object string; 13 splits unit. Equivalent. So 3,13,21 duplicates.

Also maybe 22? No.

Also 6: feature articulating LCD screen with qualifier ordinal second. 18: feature articulating LCD screen no qualifier. Are they equivalent? 6 says it's a feature and also includes ordinal "second". The paragraph says "second Canon EOS camera with an articulating LCD screen". So the fact includes that it's the second camera with that feature. 18 just says it has the feature, no ordinal. The ordinal adds extra info, so they are not equivalent because 6 conveys more info. The test: does 6 assert same complete proposition as 18? 6 asserts both that it has the feature and that it's the second such camera. 18 only asserts it has the feature. So not equivalent. Keep separate.

Also 7: supersedes Canon EOS 550D. 25 also supersedes same. So 7 and 25 duplicates.

Also 16: predecessor Canon EOS 550D with qualifier discontinued date June 2012. That's extra info beyond just predecessor. Not equivalent to supersedes.

Also 17: successor Canon EOS 650D. 27 also successor same. So 17 and 27 duplicates.

Also 9: successor relation but reversed: subject Canon EOS 650D successor object Canon EOS 600D. That's inverse of 17. Not equivalent.

payload.title: Canon EOS 600D
payload.paragraph_text: The Canon EOS 600D is an 18.0 megapixel digital single - lens reflex camera, released by Canon on 7 February 2011. It is known as the EOS Kiss X5 in Japan and the EOS Rebel T3i in the Americas. The 600D is the second Canon EOS camera with an articulating LCD screen and supersedes the 550D, although the earlier model was not discontinued until June 2012, when the successor of the 600D, the 650D, was announced.
